incident: AA22-277A: Impacket and CovalentStealer used to steal sensitive data from a Defense Industrial Base (DIB) organization; APT access to Microsoft Exchange, Impacket lateral movement, HyperBro on multiple systems (intrusion mid-Jan 2021 to mid-Jan 2022, advisory 2022-10-04)

sources.title: CISA/FBI/NSA Joint CSA AA22-277A: Impacket and Exfiltration Tool Used to Steal Sensitive Information from Defense Industrial Base Organization (2022-10-04)
sources.what_it_gave: entry point (Microsoft Exchange Server, mid-Jan 2021, vector unknown); hops (Impacket implanted on another system for lateral movement; HyperBro installed on the Exchange Server and two other systems); exfil (CovalentStealer to OneDrive, July-Oct 2021); detection (CISA IR engagement Nov 2021-Jan 2022; victim detection method not stated)

narrative_before: APT actors gained access to a DIB organization's Microsoft Exchange Server as early as mid-January 2021 (initial access vector unknown) and within four hours gathered Exchange details and ran mailbox searches using a compromised administrator account ('Admin 1') over a VPN; they returned in early February 2021, again via Admin 1 over VPN (AA22-277A). In early-to-mid February 2021 they ran Windows Command Shell discovery and collection over ~3 days, archived sensitive contract files with WinRAR renamed 'VMware.exe' split into ~3 MB chunks in the Exchange CU2\he\debug directory. In February 2021 Impacket (wmiexec.py/smbexec.py) was implanted on another system and used to attempt lateral movement. In early March 2021 the actors exploited the ProxyLogon chain (CVE-2021-26855/-26857/-26858/-27065) and installed 17 China Chopper webshells on the Exchange Server; later in March they installed HyperBro on the Exchange Server and two other systems. From late July to mid-October 2021 they used the custom CovalentStealer tool to exfiltrate remaining sensitive files to a Microsoft OneDrive folder. CISA conducted incident response from November 2021 to January 2022; the actors maintained access through mid-January 2022, likely using legitimate credentials (AA22-277A).

detection_moments.description: Mid-January 2021: initial access to the Exchange Server using compromised admin account Admin 1 over VPN; Exchange reconnaissance and mailbox searches within four hours.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Some APT actors gained initial access to the organization's Microsoft Exchange Server as early as mid-January 2021... used a compromised admin account (Admin 1) against the EWS API over a VPN' - AA22-277A

detection_moments.description: February 2021: data archived with WinRAR on the Exchange Server; Impacket implanted on another system and used to attempt lateral movement.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Impacket was implanted on another system, and the actors tried to move laterally from it'; WinRAR archives 'split into approximately 3MB chunks located on the Microsoft Exchange server' - AA22-277A

detection_moments.description: March 2021: ProxyLogon exploited, 17 China Chopper webshells on Exchange, then HyperBro installed on the Exchange Server and two other systems. (CISA engaged Nov 2021-Jan 2022; CovalentStealer exfiltration ran July-Oct 2021.)
detection_moments.evidence: 'Later in March, APT actors installed HyperBro on the Exchange Server and two other systems'; '...installed 17 China Chopper webshells on the Exchange Server' - AA22-277A

HyperBro RAT installed on one of two other systems (C2) - T1071.001 / T1105

ambiguities: Initial access vector to the Exchange Server is explicitly unknown.
The advisory names no hosts beyond roles; 'another system' and 'two other systems' are modelled as srv_impacket, srv_hyperbro_1/2. No DC is mentioned.
Direction of the Impacket and HyperBro hops (origin host) is not stated; all drawn from the Exchange beachhead.
Multiple APT groups were present; the advisory does not fully separate their actions.
Victim's own detection method is not described; only CISA's IR window (Nov 2021-Jan 2022) is given.
